newsitem.title: USA: UPS CEO flexible on key issue in Teamsters dispute.
newsitem.headline: UPS CEO flexible on key issue in Teamsters dispute.

text.p: United Parcel Service chief James Kelly appeared to show some flexibility on a key issue in the company's dispute with the Teamsters on Thursday, saying no single issue would bar agreement to end the strike.

"We think the pension issue is very important for both our people and the future of our company, but as I said there is no one or two single issues that will determine whether or not we're able to reach agreement," he told wire service reporters in a telephone interview from the company's Atlanta headquarters. The issue of whether UPS employees should put their pension money in a company plan or the Teamsters plan has become an important sticking point in the dispute.
Kelly on Wednesday declared the talks with the Teamsters at an impasse. But the company returned to talks with the union Thursday at the urging of Labor Secretary Alexis Herman.

The company had insisted that any agreement establish a new pension fund covering only UPS workers and controlled by the company and the union. That would replace the existing union pension fund, which covers Teamsters workers in more than two dozen firms, most of them truckers.

The union insists that UPS convert thousands of part-time jobs into fulltime and has tried to make that the main issue in the 11-day-old strike. Three out of five Teamsters working for UPS are now classified as part-time.
